headline: Approved a data center zoning amendment, a $12,826 CivicPlus website contract renewal, and a Saugatucket watershed study; referred a pool cover ordinance.
summary: The meeting covered board appointments, water supply, zoning, and town grants. Approved items included a data center zoning amendment, a CivicPlus contract renewal, and a $44,000 EMS grant.
decisions: Approved four appointments: Charlene Butler to the Housing Authority, Paul Carmody and David Kokette to the Canvassing Authority, and Rick Trenbath to the Saugatucket Veterans Memorial Commission.
Tabled the reappointment of Steve Stewart to the Saugatucket Veterans Memorial Park Commission until his discharge proof is received.
Approved a CivicPlus website contract renewal of $12,826, up from $11,700.
Approved the zoning ordinance amendment on data centers.
Approved items 11B and 11C on a proposed zoning change for a business park near North Second.
Approved a $44,000 federal grant to replace EMS monitors and equipment.
Approved a town manager agreement for a study of the Saugatucket watershed and flood response, using a $200,000 grant.
Approved a study of the Factory Pond wells and water supply.
Referred the pool safety cover ordinance change, which would allow automatic covers in place of fences, to Planning and Legal, 4 to 1.
Passed a motion on short-term rental rules; the transcript does not record its exact wording.
discussion: Veolia water supply: Discussion covered drought status, new test wells, and frustration over missing water records and communication.
Data center zoning: Members discussed water and electricity use, battery storage concerns, and whether a variance could still be sought.
Pool safety covers: Discussion weighed automatic covers against fences for child safety and whether the local ordinance should be updated.
Short-term rentals: Discussion covered a pending Rhode Island Supreme Court case and the need to follow the zoning process.
